name: Magnesium
short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.
text: In a Cochrane review of trials of magnesium for muscle cramps, major adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events did not differ significantly from placebo, but oral magnesium was associated with mostly gastrointestinal adverse events such as diarrhoea, reported by 11% to 37% of participants (10% to 14% with control). A clinical review states that severe hypermagnesaemia can be life-threatening but is almost exclusively seen in people with substantially decreased kidney function who take in high amounts of magnesium from supplements, laxatives or antacids. An older review of quinolone antibiotics reports that antacids containing magnesium greatly reduce quinolone absorption, probably by forming non-absorbable chelates.
